chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the exegete, al-Jarjani, may Allah be pleased with him, told us: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni told us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nasiri, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them).

He said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the abstinent in this world. He said: The one who abandons what is allowable from it out of fear of its reckoning, and who abandons its forbidden out of fear of its punishment.

key_terms.حِسَاب: Reckoning / Account (on the Day of Judgement)
key_terms.زَاهِد: Ascetic / One who abstains from worldly pleasures

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a true ascetic (zahid) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of *zuhd* (asceticism) from mere renunciation to a nuanced spiritual discipline where one avoids permissible goods out of reverence for their accountability and forbidden ones out of fear of punishment. This definition reflects the Shia emphasis on *ittiba'* (following the law) combined with *ihsan* (spiritual excellence), distinguishing the true ascetic from the negligent who ignore the world entirely. It underscores that true piety involves mindful engagement with the permissible, ensuring that even lawful acts do not become distractions from divine remembrance.
